reading_note: The teaching describes how divine operation moves through the spiritual heavens without rupturing them, and how the heavens in turn do not commingle violently with that operation. The natural image — the Wheel turning through the heavens without cleaving them, like a ship parting lions on the sea or a bird leaving no track in the air or the sun crossing the sky — corresponds to the truth that spiritual realities interpenetrate without mutual destruction. The arc moves from question (how can the Wheel turn through the heavens without piercing them?) through three analogies (ship/lions, bird/air, sun/heavens) to the answer: because spiritual things are spiritual, they pass through one another without cleaving. This is the doctrinal ground for why divine influx (the "rain" of the title) does not pour all at once but enters by gradual reception — spiritual operation does not violently rend the receiving vessel; it parts and rejoins without leaving a wound.
